transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?
What brings me in is, late at night when I start picking at leftovers, I have a hard time stopping. I’m telling myself, “That’s enough, Alejandro,” but I just keep going back for more anyway.
After one of these late-night eating episodes, do you ever try to 'make up for it'—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting the next day, or exercising a lot more than usual?
No, I don’t do anything like that afterward.
How often do these episodes of feeling unable to stop eating happen—for example, how many times per week—and how long has this been going on?
Looking back, it’s been at least once most weeks—often two nights a week—since my cousin moved in.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't control what or how much you're eating, even if you want to stop?
Yes. Once I start, I know I should stop, but it feels like my hand just keeps going back for more anyway.
During these episodes, do you often eat until you feel uncomfortably full?
Yeah. I don’t usually get sick, but I’ll eat enough that my belt feels tight, and I have to sit in my workshop chair for a while because my stomach is so uncomfortable.
Do you ever eat alone during these episodes because you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah. I wait until the house is quiet, or I’ll go out in the garage. I’d be embarrassed if my cousin or the rest of the family saw how much I was eating—especially since I’m supposed to be the disciplined one.
How many months ago did your cousin move in, and has this pattern of eating episodes continued regularly since then?
About four months ago. It started around when my older cousin moved in, and it’s kept happening regularly since then.
